properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 3:58PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
At 358 PM AST, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong
thunderstorms extending from Arecibo eastward into Florida, and is
nearly stationary. Fallen trees and power lines already reported in
the area.

HAZARD...Landspouts, wind gusts up to 40 mph, and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to outdoor objects is possible. Gusty winds
could knock down tree limbs and blow around unsecured
objects.

Locations impacted include...
Florida, Barceloneta, Manati, Ciales, Pajonal, Imbery, La Luisa, La
Alianza, Barahona, Coto Norte, Bufalo, Tiburones, Garrochales,
Tierras Nuevas Poniente, Tierras Nuevas Pon, Sabana Hoyos and
Animas.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 12 at 1:34PM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Western
Millard and Juab Counties, Bear Lake and Bear River Valley, Cache
Valley/Utah Portion, Eastern Box Elder County, Great Salt Lake
Desert and Mountains, Northern Wasatch Front, Salt Lake Valley,
Tooele and Rush Valleys, Utah Valley, Wasatch Back, Wasatch
Mountains I-80 North, Wasatch Mountains South of I-80, Western
Uinta Basin and Western Uinta Mountains. This includes recent burn
scars such as Rocky Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and recent burn scars. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage and urban areas. Extensive street flooding and flooding of
creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moisture will continue to spread into northern Utah producing a
prolonged rainfall event. In particular, moisture interacting
with a frontal boundary across far northern Utah may yield
locally heavier rainfall totals compared to other locations. As a
result, areal flooding is possible across northern Utah.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, Eastern Juab/Millard Counties, San
Rafael Swell, Sanpete Valley, Sevier Valley, Wasatch Plateau/Book
Cliffs, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef National Park and
Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell, South Central
Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper Sevier River Valleys, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County, Southwest Utah and Zion
National Park. This also includes recent burn scars such as
Forsyth, Cottonwood, Silver King, France Canyon, and Monroe Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may
occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Anomalously high moisture will continue to impact the region.
While this is expected to be a long duration rainfall event,
scattered instances of heavier rainfall rates are expected with
stronger storms yielding flash flooding concerns given saturated
soils and prior burn scars.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 12 at 8:00AM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by midweek. This trough should remain
strong and active while over the territory, and may even intensify
with embedded low pressure centers. Widespread showers may be
heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of
thunderstorms. Widespread flash flooding may occur from this
rainfall, and landslides will be possible along steep mountainous
terrain. Impacts could begin as early as Wednesday and are
expected to persist through the weekend. While there is still
uncertainty in the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan
now for wet conditions that could start as early as Wednesday and
persist through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 10:59AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Thursday into the weekend, a series of low pressure systems will
move toward Southeast Alaska, bringing widespread moderate to heavy
rainfall and gale force winds to the Gulf. Strong winds are also
expected for coastal communities. While the exact timing and impacts
of the system are still being refined, confidence is continuing to
increase that this will be a more impactful system for Southeast
Alaska.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
developing situation and update our forecast.

properties.areaDesc: Owens Valley North
properties.headline: Freeze Watch issued October 12 at 11:53AM PDT until October 14 at 10:00AM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 30 possible.

* WHERE...Northern Owens Valley.

* WHEN...Cancelled for Monday Night into Tuesday Morning... Reissued
for Tuesday Night into Wednesday Morning.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increased cloud cover will remain persistent
through the start of the overnight period tonight along with
elevated gusty winds ahead of an incoming cold front. As a result,
temperatures in the northern Owens Valley are likely to remain
above-freezing tonight. The Freeze Watch has been pushed back to
Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, when winds will be lighter
and skies will be clear.
properties.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

To prevent water pipes from freezing; wrap or drain or allow them to
drip slowly.
